context: ProofWiki source is the general group-homomorphism kernel; specialize to abelian groups and their additive identities without identifying the subset as literally an abstract categorical universal arrow.
editorial_note: ProofWiki source is the general group-homomorphism kernel; specialize to abelian groups and their additive identities without identifying the subset as literally an abstract categorical universal arrow.
text: For an abelian-group homomorphism f:A→B, ker(f)={a∈A:f(a)=0_B}, an additive subgroup of A.

context: Stacks Definition 12.3.9 item 1. Kernel is a universal arrow unique up to unique isomorphism; it need not exist for all morphisms of a preadditive category.
editorial_note: Stacks Definition 12.3.9 item 1. Kernel is a universal arrow unique up to unique isomorphism; it need not exist for all morphisms of a preadditive category.
text: Given f:x→y in a preadditive category, a kernel is a morphism i:k→x satisfying f∘i=0 such that every j:z→x with f∘j=0 factors uniquely as j=i∘h.

context: Stacks Definition 12.3.9 item 3. The universal arrow exists only for morphisms admitting cokernels, and in the category of abelian groups represents quotient by the image.
editorial_note: Stacks Definition 12.3.9 item 3. The universal arrow exists only for morphisms admitting cokernels, and in the category of abelian groups represents quotient by the image.
text: For f:x→y in a preadditive category, a cokernel is a morphism p:y→c with p∘f=0 such that every q:y→z with q∘f=0 factors uniquely as q=h∘p.

context: Stacks Definition 12.5.7. An additive category alone is not enough for the given image-equals-kernel formulation; abelian-group sequences form a special case.
editorial_note: Stacks Definition 12.5.7. An additive category alone is not enough for the given image-equals-kernel formulation; abelian-group sequences form a special case.
text: A sequence of morphisms in an abelian category is exact at its interior object Y of X→Y→Z when the image of X→Y equals the kernel of Y→Z; successive compositions are zero. A short exact sequence has the form 0→A→B→C→0.
